title: Digital health tools for health education and information access in low and middle-income countries (LMICs) affected by humanitarian crises: A scoping review protocol
content:
by Niaz Ahmed, Elysée Nouvet, Saleema Allana, Anam Shahil-Feroz, Anushka Ataullahjan

Humanitarian crises disrupt health services and access to reliable information in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Mobile-enabled digital tools may reach affected communities, but evidence on the technologies used, implementation contexts, and equitable access is dispersed. This scoping review will map empirical evidence on mobile-enabled digital tools used to deliver health education, health promotion, risk communication, or health information to crisis-affected populations in LMICs. The review will follow Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) scoping review guidance and will be reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The Population, Concept, Context framework will guide eligibility. English-language empirical publications and data-bearing grey literature issued from January 2010 through the final search date will be included. The planned sources are MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, the Nursing and Allied Health Database, Sociology Collection, Google Scholar, and specified humanitarian agency repositories. Search strategies and individual run logs will be retained. Two reviewers will independently screen records. One reviewer will chart the data, and a second reviewer will verify all charted fields against source documents. The review will classify tool types and multifunctional interventions, describe implementation features and equity factors, and map reported trust, acceptability, adoption, knowledge, and access outcomes. A hybrid deductive and inductive approach will be used for thematic analysis. Results will be summarized descriptively without meta-analysis or causal claims. Search histories, eligibility decisions, the charting dataset, and analysis materials will be deposited in a public Open Science Framework (OSF) repository, subject to any justified third-party restrictions. The protocol is registered on OSF (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/MZRWQ).
